q-112202.name: Question 1
q-112202.problem:
Find the vector $x$, if $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ and 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -8 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
q-112202.worked_solution:
We know that any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -8 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,B.$ Since we are told that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -8 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{{(\,-3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -24 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -12 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -36 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We know that any vector in Span{b1,b2} has the form

x1[1−81]+x2[241]

where x1 and x2 are the coordinates relative to the basis B. Since we are told that [x]B=[3−3], we obtain

x=(3)⏟x1[1−81]+(−3)⏟x2[241]=[3−243]+[−6−12−3]=[−3−360].

q-35232.name: Question 2
q-35232.problem:
Find the vector $x$, if $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ and 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$
q-35232.worked_solution:
We know that any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,B.$ Since we are told that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(\,-3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{{(\,5\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 6 \\ -9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}25 \\ 15 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 \\ 21 \\ 11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-112208.name: Question 3
q-112208.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{2}?$
q-112208.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,2\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}+{{(\,6\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{3}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{3}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=2\cdot {b}_{1}+3\cdot {b}_{2}+6\cdot {b}_{3}
$$

and therefore 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 6\end{aligned}],
$$

Finally, ${x}_{2}=3.$

q-75972.name: Question 4
q-75972.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}?$
q-75972.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,-6\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,4\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=(-6)\cdot {b}_{1}+4\cdot {b}_{2}
$$

and therefore

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we have that ${x}_{1}=-6.$

?

Find the coordinates of the vector x relative to the basis B={b1,b2}, where b1=[01],b2=[10],x=[4−6]. If [x]B=[x1x2] then what is the value of x1?

a
4
b
−6
c
10
d
−2
e
2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that

[4−6]⏟x=(−6)⏟x1⋅[01]⏟b1+(4)⏟x2⋅[10]⏟b2

which means that

x=(−6)⋅b1+4⋅b2

and therefore

[x]B=[−64].

Finally, we have that x1=−6.

q-112247.name: Question 5
q-112247.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
q-112247.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -3 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -3 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & 15\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=2 \\ -5{x}_{2}=15.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-3.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-2(-3)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-4.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-4)+(-3)=-7.$

q-112213.name: Question 6
q-112213.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 20\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
q-112213.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 4 & -2 & 20\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 4 & -2 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & -10 & 40\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-5 \\ -10{x}_{2}=40.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-4.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+2(-4)=-5\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3+(-4)=-1.$

q-76056.name: Question 7
q-76056.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
q-76056.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that  

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-5){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & -6 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 25 & -25\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

  

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-4 \\ 25{x}_{3}=-25.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this into the second   equation yields

$$
{x}_{2}+3(-1)=-4\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-1.
$$

 Finally,  by substituting ${x}_{2}=-1$ and ${x}_{3}=-1$ into the first equation we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+(-1)-(-1)=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

So, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1+(-1)+(-1)=-1.
$$

q-34764.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
q-34764.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & -1 & -9 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 
The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=2 \\ 2{x}_{2}=4 \\ -{x}_{3}=-1 \\ 0=4,\end{aligned}
$$

where the fourth equation is always false. Therefore, the system has no solution and we conclude that 

$$
x\notin \text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}.
$$
